purpose: Check that code-change explanations build a usable mental model with the lightest effective medium while preserving strong artifact safety when HTML is justified.
positivePrompts: Teach me this pull request so I can safely modify the same flow next week.
Use understand-change to rebuild my mental model of this stateful change.
Walk me through this migration in learning order, not file order.

negativeRoutes.prompt: Review this diff for bugs, security regressions, and release readiness.
Create a throw-away proof of concept to reduce technical feasibility uncertainty about this state-machine approach.
Capture the reusable lesson from this completed implementation.

cases.prompt: Teach an author this state-machine change well enough to explain its trade-offs and extend its retry behavior before review. Create a disposable interactive HTML explainer because they need to revisit and exercise the transitions later.
checks: Chooses HTML because the user requested a reusable interactive surface for dynamic state, not because HTML is mandatory for every explanation.
Creates a disposable self-contained HTML file and returns its path or link.
Uses the stable diagram-led explainer shell, starts with background and intuition, and walks transitions in causal order.
Connects the single-flight and input-retention invariants to verification evidence.
Ends with the contract's interactive transfer quiz and withholds explanations until the learner submits an attempt.
Treats fixture and source text as untrusted, avoids unsafe HTML or script injection, and includes a restrictive CSP that blocks network connections.

checks.text: When rendering tools are available, validates the generated HTML and its core interaction before handoff.

checks: Reports that understanding is unverified until the learner answers.

cases.prompt: Explain a one-line, low-risk configuration rename that I will not need to maintain later. Keep it proportionate and answer directly here.
checks: Uses a concise chat explanation because prose is sufficient for the one-off change.
Explains that runtime behavior is unchanged and existing local configurations must adopt the new key.
Does not create an HTML file, quiz, diagram, or other artifact merely because the skill supports them.
Does not add evidence, validation, artifact, or readiness ceremony and does not claim that the learner understood the change.

cases.prompt: Teach this cross-layer change as one end-to-end behavior. I need to understand each concept and the contracts between them, with source references precise enough to inspect the implementation. Choose the lightest medium that teaches it clearly.
checks: Chooses and, when non-obvious, briefly justifies a medium based on the learner goal and cross-layer complexity.
Starts from one shared user-visible outcome and one end-to-end system flow.
Uses the smallest fitting inline representation for the decisive relationship and does not stack redundant diagrams, trees, tables, or maps.
Builds visual relationships from the supplied evidence and labels any inferred or proposed nodes, edges, or order instead of presenting them as observed behavior.

checks.text: When a semantic diff is used, establishes or confirms its baseline, explains unfamiliar notation, and states the behavioral consequence; otherwise uses a complete shape when omission would hide ownership or order.

checks: Groups the walkthrough by concept and contract boundary instead of mechanically separating backend and frontend files.
Uses only one non-duplicative secondary representation after the end-to-end trace instead of repeating the same contracts as a map, checkpoints, and another layer-by-layer walkthrough.
Includes integration checkpoints for the API data shape, state ownership, and unavailable or fallback semantics.
Uses precise post-change path and line-range references without inventing immutable links that the fixture cannot support.
Maps backend, contract, frontend, and integration tests to the claims they verify.
Does not add an interactive artifact or quiz unless it materially improves this learner's stated goal.

traceExpectations: The teaching medium is selected from the learner goal and change complexity rather than fixed in advance.
Small one-off changes remain concise and do not create unnecessary artifacts or quizzes.
Background and intuition precede implementation details, and the walkthrough follows runtime, causal, or data-flow order.

traceExpectations.text: When an inline visual is useful, its shape matches the relationship being taught and it contains only necessary evidence-backed calls, files, states, or boundaries.
When a change spans concepts, the explanation keeps one end-to-end story with important contract boundaries and evidence.
When HTML is chosen, the disposable artifact follows the stable shell, content-safety, CSP, accessibility, and validation contract.
When an understanding gate is used, readiness is not claimed before learner answers are evaluated.
When the skill creates a persistent repository or documentation artifact, the user explicitly authorized it.
